WV-2026-HB5693.title: Supplemental appropriation, Department of Tourism Revenue

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 663)

WV-2026-HB5693.aiSummary: Approved by the governor, this law makes a supplemental appropriation, or extra funding, from Department of Tourism revenue. It affects the Department of Tourism and how that money is used.

WV-2026-HB5288.title: Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of Agriculture-West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund from Special Revenue
WV-2026-HB5288.aiSummary: This bill would add $200,000 in special revenue to the West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund in the Department of Agriculture for fiscal year 2026. The money would be for current expenses in that program. It was approved by the governor and became law.

WV-2026-HB4412.title: Require certain websites to utilize age verification methods to prevent minors from accessing content

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amend with amend, passed bill (Roll No. 599)
Senate concurred in House amendments and passed bill (Roll No. 685)
Passed Senate with amended title (Roll No. 397)
Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

votes.motion: Senate concurred in House amendments and passed bill

WV-2026-HB4412.aiSummary: West Virginia passed a law that requires some websites and other online businesses that offer material harmful to minors to check a user’s age before showing that content. It creates civil liability, or the chance to be sued, for publishers and distributors that do not use the required age checks, and it allows the Attorney General to bring cases too. It also sets rules for keeping data, civil penalties, and some exceptions for internet service providers and hosting companies that did not create the material.

WV-2026-HB4106.aiSummary: This law lets people ages 18 to 20 carry a concealed deadly weapon, which means a hidden weapon, without first getting a license. It also removes a crime tied to carrying a deadly weapon without a license for some people under 21 and changes the rules for minors who may lawfully possess or carry a firearm in certain cases. The law also sets misdemeanor and other criminal penalties for a minor who is convicted of unlawfully carrying a deadly weapon.

WV-2026-HB5684.aiSummary: The law lets the state Supreme Court create child protection commissioners to handle child protection cases. It sets rules for who can serve, how they are appointed and supervised, what they can do, and how they are paid. It also gives some retirement benefit rules for certain retired public workers who take these jobs and lets senior judges and justices serve as commissioners.

WV-2026-HB5480.aiSummary: The law sets up a West Virginia youth summer job and career readiness program. It lets the state work with local agencies, give grant money to employer partners, and use a special fund, grants, and donations to support the program. It also requires yearly reports and sets rules for how the program runs.

WV-2026-HB5048.title: To ensure virtual instruction for foster students while in temporary placement facilities.

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 673)

WV-2026-HB5048.aiSummary: The law requires foster children who are waiting for a new placement to keep getting school through virtual learning. It sets rules for which county provides that learning, gives state education tech training to the person or group caring for the child, and says virtual classes should start within three days. When the child is placed with a foster family, school and login info must be sent to the family and the new county.

WV-2026-HB4865.title: Providing for a program allowing election official trainees to be appointed as election officials

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 672)
Passed Senate with amended title (Roll No. 549)
Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

WV-2026-HB4865.aiSummary: The law lets local election leaders create a program for high school juniors and seniors, including home-schooled students, to train and serve as election officials. These students must meet set voting, age, school, approval, and training rules, and only one such trainee may serve per party in each precinct. The law also lets county leaders suspend an election official’s ability to serve for certain problems, such as not showing up, bad conduct, or interfering with voters.

WV-2026-HB4850.title: Providing online training for Executors/Executrix of an Estate

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 654)

WV-2026-HB4850.aiSummary: The law provides online training for people who handle an estate, called executors or executrixes. It affects people serving in that role in West Virginia. It was approved by the governor and became Chapter 110 in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4625.title: Relating to quit claim deeds

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 640)

WV-2026-HB4625.aiSummary: The law changes rules for the real estate transfer tax in West Virginia. It says quitclaim deeds are not counted as taxable transfer documents under this chapter. It also changes some tax rules and definitions for people recording deeds and other property transfer papers.

WV-2026-HB4577.aiSummary: The law ties driver’s license and ID card applications to voter registration updates at DMV offices. It also sets rules for sending that voter information to election officials, protecting some of it as private, and says people can opt out of voter registration. It also lets West Virginia recognize driver’s licenses from Ireland and Japan through reciprocal agreements, if those countries meet certain standards.

WV-2026-HB4463.aiSummary: The law changes the powers and duties of the Board of Sanitarians, including setting fees, giving and renewing licenses and certificates, running exams, and handling complaints and discipline. It also sets rules for sanitarian, sanitarian-in-training, and registered sanitarian qualifications, including education, work experience, training hours, and online or in-person training. It lets qualified out-of-state applicants get a West Virginia license or certificate without an exam if they meet certain conditions, and the board must adopt the state’s 2025 universal reciprocity rules by May 1, 2026.

WV-2026-HB4025.aiSummary: The law changes how some new hires and promoted employees in the Departments of Health Facilities, Human Services, and Health are handled under the state civil service system. It moves those workers into the classified exempt system, which means they are not in the usual civil service job system. The bill became law in 2026.
